page.overview:
Who is Colin Davis?

Colin Davis (born 29 July 1933 and died 19 December 2012) was a British racing driver who participated in two Formula One races with Scuderia Centro Sud driving a in . He was also a two-time class leader at the 24 Hours of Le Mans.

Davis is the son of British racing driver Sammy Davis, who won the 1927 24 Hours of Le Mans and earned two class victories in 1925 and 1927.

He was an advertising executive who raced a Formula 3 . He eventually moved to Italy and began his racing career with in the 1958 24 Hours of Le Mans, where he earned his first class victory. The team also entered him into the 1958 Argentine Grand Prix, although Davis did not participate in the event.

In , Davis drove a Cooper for Scuderia Centro Sud in the French and Italian Grand Prix. In France he had an oil leak early in the race that forced him to retire and in Italy he finished 11th. These were his only two Formula One participations, although he did take part in some non-championship races in the years that followed.
